To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) novice ontology authors benefit from guidance about their ontology authoring process, (ii) they benefit from understandable syntax error messages to find the correct CNL, (iii) they benefit from feedback about the integration into an existing ontology, (iv) they benefit from guidance to use the right terminology in their ontologies, and (v) they benefit from a dialogue system to interact with an ontology authoring system.

the following intelligent tool support can help domain experts to author ontologies using a CNL: (1) providing guidance about ontology engineering methodologies, (2) providing feedback about the logical consequences and (3) providing feedback about syntactical errors and the integration of the author’s input into the ontology.
domain experts can author ontologies with a CNL-based authoring system when provided with intelligent tool support.
In summary, our research is concerned with

making ontology authoring more intuitive by providing intelligent support to novice ontology authors and by studying how this support impacts the ontology author’s understanding of and ability to use ontologies.
the design and evaluation of intelligent tool support to facilitate the authoring of ontologies by domain experts.
how to make the ontology authoring task more accessible to domain users, and in particular, to novice ontology authors who are not knowledge engineers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
intelligent tool support can make ontology authorship more intuitive and accessible to domain experts, although it is still not yet possible to completely automate the process.

CNL-based ontology authors can benefit from tool support for understanding the syntax and semantics of their ontology authoring language, following ontology engineering methodologies, understanding the logical consequences of their additions to an ontology and interacting with the ontology system via dialogues.

CNL-based ontology editing systems can make ontology editing more accessible to domain users if they provide intelligent tool support for (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv), and the tool support is designed in a way that the user can easily understand the feedback provided by the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a controlled natural language as an ontology authoring interface is a promising way for domain experts to write ontologies.
we have provided the foundations for a new approach for building ontology authoring tools that can help domain experts to write their own ontologies without having to learn a new syntax or formalism.
the use of a controlled natural language and intelligent tool support can indeed help domain experts to author ontologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

intelligent tool support for ontology authoring using CNL can make this task accessible for non-experts, but the tool support has to be tailored to the needs of the domain experts, and it should be provided as a natural dialogue between the domain expert and the ontology authoring tool.

intelligent tool support for ontology authoring can help novice ontology authors to overcome some of the main barriers to writing ontologies, but that the design of such tool support requires a deep understanding of the ontology authoring task, and that the tool support needs to be designed iteratively and evaluated in practice to be effective.
intelligent tool support for novice ontology authors can significantly alleviate the syntactical burden of writing ontologies.
